Made in China. Nice but make sure you have the right expectations. - There are a lot of these countertop icemakers being sold by Chinese companies on Amazon right now. Most of them work exactly the same, though they may look slightly different. But you need to make sure you understand exactly how they work before purchasing. As long as your expectations meet what the actual icemaker will do, then you will be fine.

The listing shows that this ice machine makes 26 pounds of ice in a twenty-four hour period. That is only possible if you remove the ice each time the bin is full. The bin holds enough ice to fill a 32 ounce water bottle. It takes approximately one hour for the bin to fill. So someone would have to remove the ice day and night to actually make 26 pounds worth of ice. If you do not remove the eyes, then it simply melts and is recycled again and again. The ice is not kept frozen inside the machine. The only way to keep the ice frozen would be to remove it and place it in your own freezer. On top of this, the ice is “wet” and will freeze together if you place it in your own freezer. So you will need to break it apart to use it. Also, this ice machine is not connected to a water source. You must pour water into the machine for it to make ice.

By ice maker in my freezer stopped working a while ago. But the overall refrigerator freezer works just fine. So having this separate icemaker works for me. I know some others who use them in a small office environment… And a motorhome… And so on.

This ice machine is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. Again, there are several Chinese companies selling similar ice machines on Amazon right now. So look around before purchasing for the best price. Some also offer a timer, which is nice so that the ice machine is not operating when you are sleeping. Otherwise, if you leave it on at night, then the ice will simply refreeze again and again.

water filter fix - There have been many reviews written stating that filters for the LT1000-PC not fitting.
The issue is that lg has a defect that have not been addressed or recalled leading to consumer's confusion.
This has to do with the 2 groove heads on the refrigerator not aligning properly with the grooves on the filter.
There are many posts on this.
The best one I found is to file down the notches on the side of an old filter using sandpaper or nail filer and marking a line on the side of the filter to help with alignment.
Then we use the old filter to rotate the grooves head counterclockwise to the correct horizontal position of 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock.

After installing this filter, I have noticed a taste improvement compared unfiltered regular tap water.

I love this icemaker! - I've had this icemaker for about 8 months, and I absolutely love it. The cubes are small, and if I turn it off when its full and let it sit for a for about half an hour, the ice becomes very 'soft' - I don't know quite how else to describe it - perfect for someone like me who loves to eat ice. It makes 9 cubes about every 8 minutes, which might seem like a long time, but the basket is always full when I'm ready for more. When it's full (it's small), it will completely fill up 2 16-ounce glasses, plus some. I tried at first to keep some in the freezer, but that didn't work too well. The ice sticks together and unless you think to stir it around every 5 minutes for a few times, you get lumps of ice instead of individual cubes. If you're just refillng an ice bucket, it's great. If you want to have a good stash of ice in the freezer, not so much. I live alone, so it's perfect or me. For more than 2, maybe 3 people, I think you'd really need something different. Just my opinion; I suppose you could make it work if you don't have any serious ice-eaters. Anyhow I love it. It's certainly paid for itself a few times over already. The one and only flaw, as far as I'm concerned, is that the lid will hit you in the head (if, like me, you get that close) if you bump it when it's open. Annoying, but not a very big deal. It does require cleaning every few weeks. It recommends using vinegar, I assume to discourage mold, so I use a very weak vinegar/water solution, wipe it dry, and there's no taste. It's worked well for me. I don't use the drain plug because it's too much trouble. I just bought a turkey baster to suck most of the last of the water out and a few paper towels. Cleaning takes about 5-10 minutes. No problems so far.
I highly recommend this ice maker for anyone who loves ice or just has no ice maker in their fridge. I don't think you'll ever regret it.

The stove is gorgeous and I'm glad to get rid of those pesky knobs that make cleaning the sleek stove surface awkward. Lights indicate hot burners even during the cool down phase. Activating the safety lock prevents accidental touches from turning on burners.

DOWNSIDES:

The true exterior dimensions of this stove are 20-7/8 X 29-3/4. This proved a minor issue since my Jenn-Air used a slightly larger cutout.

For crying out loud, GE, include a set of wire nuts and maybe a conduit connector! They cost almost nothing. I reused my old wire nuts, but come on.

BIGGEST PROBLEM: The GE JP5030SJSS places a big honkin' box at the bottom rear of the stove, plus the overall thickness measures considerably more than my Jenn-Air or a standard coil burner stove. You are either going to have to retrofit your stove drawers or remove face plates, attach them to the cabinet and kiss off your drawers. I cut off about four inches from my drawer backs and shaved off half an inch from the top edges, but many people don't have the tools or experience for this retrofit. Be warned!
